subject: Mobile Development
title: Why Thirty Percent?
description: Learn Why Thirty Percent? in one minute.

hook.text: Apple and Google each take 30% of every app sale and in-app purchase. Why that number?

buildup.text: The 30% cut mirrors what brick-and-mortar retail traditionally charged for shelf space.

discovery.text: Apple says the fee covers hosting, review, payment processing, and fraud protection.

twist.text: Critics call it a monopoly tax. Credit card fees are only 2-3%. Hosting costs are pennies.

climax.text: The 30% commission is the single most debated policy in the entire app economy.

punchline.text: Thirty cents of every dollar goes to the platform.

quiz.question: What do critics say about the 30% commission?
options: It's a monopoly tax far exceeding actual costs
It's too low for the service provided
